title: All in One: Multi-Task Prompting for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Graph tasks at node, edge, and graph levels are highly diversified.

gap.claim: Pre-training pretexts can be incompatible with multiple graph tasks and may cause negative transfer to specific applications.

contributions.claim: A multi-task prompting method for graph models is proposed.
The method unifies graph and language prompt formats through prompt tokens, token structure, and inserting patterns.
The method studies the task space of graph applications, reformulates downstream problems as graph-level tasks, and uses meta-learning to learn an initialization for multi-task graph prompts.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their multi-task prompting method for graph models as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report conducting extensive experiments.
The authors report that the experimental results demonstrate the superiority of their method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Pre-training and fine-tuning are presented as a standard workflow for graph tasks because general graph knowledge can alleviate limited application-specific annotations.
Diverse node-, edge-, and graph-level tasks make pre-training pretexts potentially incompatible, with possible negative transfer.
Prompt learning in NLP motivates prompting for graphs to bridge pre-trained models and varied graph tasks.
The proposed framework unifies graph and language prompt formats, reformulates downstream problems as graph-level tasks, and applies meta-learning for prompt initialization.
The authors report extensive experiments showing superiority of the method.

source_observation.claim: Different graph task levels can make a shared pre-training pretext incompatible and can produce negative transfer.

interpretation.claim: A reusable graph-learning framework should explicitly account for task heterogeneity and transfer failure modes.

application.claim: When adapting a pre-trained graph model across task levels, consider prompt-based task reformulation and task-aware initialization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy works for every graph task or application.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The prompt architecture, task-space formulation, and meta-learning procedure are not detailed.
No limitations, computational costs, or independent verification are reported.
